definitions.explanation: A pair of sticks used for eating in Japan and other Asian countries.

examples.japanese: {箸|はし}を{使|つか}って{食|た}べてください。
{箸|はし}の{使|つか}い{方|かた}がわかりますか。
examples.english: Do you know how to use chopsticks?

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}ではご{飯|はん}を{箸|はし}の{中|なか}に{立|た}てることはマナー{違反|いはん}とされています。
examples.english: In Japan, sticking chopsticks upright in rice is considered a breach of etiquette.

notes:
{箸|はし} are the essential eating utensils in Japan. お{箸|はし} is the polite form.

TYPES:
- {割|わ}り{箸|ばし}: disposable wooden chopsticks
- {塗|ぬ}り{箸|ばし}: lacquered chopsticks
- マイ{箸|はし}: personal chopsticks (brought from home)

ETIQUETTE:
- Never stick {箸|はし} upright in rice (associated with funerals)
- Don't pass food chopstick-to-chopstick (also funeral-related)
- Don't point with {箸|はし}
- Rest {箸|はし} on the {箸置|はしお}き (chopstick rest)

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {箸|はし}を{使|つか}う: to use chopsticks
- {箸|はし}が{進|すす}む: to eat with good appetite
- {箸|はし}にも{棒|ぼう}にもかからない: completely useless (idiom)
